problems.title: A point on the square-function graph
problems.question: Which listed point is on y=x²?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: A graph point must satisfy y=x².
steps: For x=√3−1, its square is 3−2√3+1=4−2√3, exactly the listed ordinate.
The other points do not have their listed y equal to x²; in particular (√2−1)²=3−√8, not √8−3.

problems.title: Which line intersects a parabola?
problems.question: Which listed line intersects y=x²?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: For y=mx+b, intersections solve x²−mx−b=0, with discriminant m²+4b.
steps: For y=x+6, the discriminant is 1+24=25>0, giving two intersections. The other five lines have negative discriminants.
Indeed x²=x+6 has roots −2 and 3.

problems.title: Two points on a parabola
problems.question: Two points on y=x² have abscissas totaling 6 and ordinates totaling 26. Find the absolute ordinate difference.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: uv=(36−26)/2=5. Thus the inputs are the roots of t²−6t+5=0, namely 1 and 5.
The ordinates are 1 and 25, differing by 24.

problems.title: Three standard triangle construction data sets
problems.question: Which allow straightedge-and-compass construction: three sides; two sides and included angle; one side and its adjacent angles?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: The standard congruence constructions are SSS,SAS,ASA.
steps: SSS uses intersecting circles at the side endpoints. SAS copies the included angle then marks both side lengths. ASA copies the two endpoint angles and intersects their rays.
Each works when the given data describe a nondegenerate triangle (triangle inequalities and valid angles).
problems.answer: All three, for valid triangle data.

problems.title: Construct three lengths from two segments
problems.question: Given positive lengths a,b, which can be constructed: (a+b)/2, √(ab), √(a²+b²)?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Midpoint construction; altitude theorem; Pythagorean theorem.
steps: Lay the segments end to end and bisect for the arithmetic mean. For √(ab), draw a semicircle on diameter a+b and erect a perpendicular at their junction; its height squares to ab.
Construct perpendicular legs a,b to obtain a hypotenuse √(a²+b²).

problems.title: A sum of absolute-value roots
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of |x−3|=11.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: The roots are 14 and −8. Their sum is 6.

problems.title: Squared sum of two quadratic roots
problems.question: x₁,x₂ solve x²−2x−13=0. Find x₁²+x₂².
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: The squared sum is 2²−2(−13)=30.

problems.title: Scalene obtuse triangles from four lengths
problems.question: Use lengths 2,3,4,5 to form all triangles. How many scalene ones are obtuse?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: For sorted a<b<c, require a+b>c and c²>a²+b².
steps: The four distinct-side triples are (2,3,4),(2,3,5),(2,4,5),(3,4,5).
The second is degenerate; the last is right. The first and third are obtuse since 16>13 and 25>20. Repeated-side triangles would not be scalene.

problems.title: A listed third side making an acute triangle
problems.question: Which of 5,6,7,11,12,13 can complete sides 6,10 to an acute triangle?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Acuteness requires each squared side smaller than the other two squares together.
steps: 100<36+a² gives a>8, while a²<136 gives a<√136≈11.66. The remaining condition and triangle inequalities hold in this interval.
Only 11 is listed inside it.

problems.title: Find a polynomial divisible by a linear factor
problems.question: Which listed polynomial is divisible by x−2?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Factor theorem: x−2 divides P(x) iff P(2)=0.
steps: For x⁴−8x, P(2)=16−16=0. The other listed expressions at 2 are 8,14,−4,−8,64, all nonzero.
Indeed x⁴−8x=x(x³−8)=x(x−2)(x²+2x+4).

problems.title: An identity valid at every positive input
problems.question: Which listed rational equality holds for every positive x?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Factor numerator and denominator, preserving their domains.
steps: $(x^2+8x+7)/(x^2+6x+5)=(x+1)(x+7)/[(x+1)(x+5)]=(x+7)/(x+5)$. Both denominators are nonzero for every x>0.
The other apparently cancellable option excludes x=1 and x=2, so cannot hold at every positive input as worded.

problems.title: Compare coefficients of two products
problems.question: (x−5)(x−p)=(x+3)(x+q) identically. Find p+q.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: The x coefficients give −5−p=3+q, so p+q=−8. Constants give 5p=3q, consistent with p=−3,q=−5.

problems.title: A median ratio forces a right triangle
problems.question: In ABC, CM is a median and CA/6=CB/8=CM/5. Find cos B.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: Scale to CA=6,CB=8,CM=5. Then AB²=2×36+2×64−4×25=100, so AB=10.
The triangle is right at C, giving cos B=CB/AB=8/10=4/5.

problems.title: A coordinate angle cosine
problems.question: A=(3,0),B=(5,0),C=(5,4). Find cos BAC.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: AB=(2,0),AC=(2,4). The dot product is 4, and length product is 2√20. The quotient is 1/√5.

problems.title: Integer roots restrict a coefficient
problems.question: Which listed a makes x²+ax−2=0 have integer roots?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: The only unordered integer root pairs are (1,−2) and (−1,2), with sums −1 and 1. Therefore a=1 or −1.
Only a=1 appears in the choices, giving roots 1 and −2.

problems.title: A relation between root sum and product
problems.question: Roots x₁,x₂ of x²−3x+a=0 satisfy x₁x₂+3x₁+3x₂=5. Find a.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: Vieta: root sum 3 and product a.
steps: Substitute into the condition: a+3×3=5. Thus a=−4, and the roots 4,−1 are real and satisfy it.

problems.title: A reciprocal substitution with a repeated root
problems.question: Find the product of real roots of x²+x+1/x+1/x²=4.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: For x≠0, put t=x+1/x; then x²+1/x²=t²−2.
steps: t²+t−6=(t−2)(t+3)=0. For t=2, (x−1)²=0 gives the single distinct root 1.
For t=−3, x²+3x+1=0 gives two real roots whose product is 1. The total distinct-root product is 1×1=1.

problems.title: Diagonal ratios from the parallelogram law
problems.question: A parallelogram’s shorter diagonal is √2 times its shorter side. Find longer-diagonal/longer-side.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: If b is the shorter side and d₁²=2b², subtracting gives d₂²=2a². Thus d₂/a=√2.

problems.title: A cevian characterized by its squared length
problems.question: In scalene ABC, L lies on AC and BL²=AB·BC−AL·LC. Must BL be a median, bisector or altitude?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: Put BC=a,AB=c,AL=u,LC=v. Equating gives a²u+c²v=ac(u+v), or (a−c)(au−cv)=0.
Scalene means a≠c, hence u/v=c/a=AB/BC. By the converse angle-bisector theorem, BL bisects B.
A median or altitude is not forced in a scalene triangle.
problems.answer: Only the angle-bisector condition is necessary.

problems.title: Two speeds on equal halves of a journey
problems.question: A cyclist covers 120 km in 9 hours, slowing by 3 km/h for the second half. Find the first-half speed.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: Clearing denominators gives 3v²−49v+60=0, or (3v−4)(v−15)=0.
The root 4/3 is too small; v=15 is valid, with times 4 and 5 hours.

problems.title: A golden-ratio segment
problems.question: A,B,C occur in that order, BC=1 and AB/BC=BC/AC. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: x=1/(x+1) gives x²+x−1=0. The positive root is (√5−1)/2.

problems.title: Count roots of a squared absolute value
problems.question: How many roots does x²−4x+4=|x−2| have?
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: u=0 gives x=2; u=1 gives x=1,3. There are three distinct roots.

problems.title: A circumdiameter in a six-eight-ten triangle
problems.question: A triangle has sides 6,8,10. Find its circumcircle diameter.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: The converse Pythagorean theorem and Thales’ theorem.
steps: 6²+8²=10², so the triangle is right. Its hypotenuse is the circle diameter, 10.

problems.title: Circumradius from an altitude and two base angles
problems.question: An altitude is 1 and the other two vertex angles are 30°,45°. Find the circumradius.
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
formulas: A side adjacent to the 30° base angle has length 1/sin30°; sine rule $c=2R\sin C$.
steps: That side is 2 and is opposite the 45° angle. Hence R=2/(2sin45°)=√2.

problems.title: Reduce a rational expression using a quadratic condition
problems.question: m²−8m−7=0. Evaluate (m²+2m−1)/(m²−3m−4).
problems.idea: Use an exact algebraic or geometric relation, then verify the conditions.
steps: The numerator becomes 10m+6 and denominator 5m+3. Their ratio is 2.
The denominator cannot vanish: m=−3/5 does not satisfy m²−8m−7=0.
